decision_clause: Ruled out: keeping the lane counts as a floor. Reason given: "two cases of slack let whole test cases and five allowlists be removed without a failure" — i.e. a lower-bound (>=) comparison on per-lane test counts permits silent deletion of test cases and allowlist entries, so the counts must be pinned exactly.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so nothing in the recorded scope changed. In the finished tree, `tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs` (the `focused-lane-is-not-silently-empty` case) still runs each focused pattern through `npm test -w @aos/schema` and compares the reported pass count to a hard-coded per-lane number with `assert.equal(Number(passed[1]), cases, ...)` — an exact-match comparison against the pinned list `[metric-registry 23, issuance-contract 17, capability 19, scoring-contract 20, session-class 28, doctor-contract 41, prescription-input 15, trace-schema 19, result-schema 19, treatment-registry 15]` — plus `assert.equal(Number(failed[1]), 0)`. A lane that loses (or gains) a case fails, not just one that drops below a bound. No `>=`, `assert.ok(count > n)`, tolerance, or slack term is applied to any lane count. `tests/planning-contract.test.mjs` likewise still pins the census literals inside fully anchored regexes (`control_plane_code_files=17 control_plane_allowlist=17 ... banned_wording_scan=on\n?$`), so the allowlist size is an exact expected string rather than a lower bound. The only `>=` comparisons in the scope files are pre-existing object-field-shape guards in `packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts` (`runtimeFields.length >= 7`, `rowFields.length >= 11`, `cellFields.length >= 7`, `definitionFields.length >= 4`) and index/offset sanity checks (`start >= 0`); none of these are lane counts.
rationale: The decision rules out one specific shape: lane counts asserted as a floor. Judging the finished tree against that, the tree does the opposite — the lane-count assertion is an exact equality with a zero-failure companion check, and the source comment at the site states the intent directly ("Exact, not a floor: a lane that loses a case must fail here"). The allowlist/census literals in the other in-scope test file are also exact anchored strings, so the second half of the recorded reason (five allowlists removable without a failure) has no purchase either. Separately, `diff.patch` is empty, so the implementation introduced no change at all in the recorded scope: the task's requirement — reject a `derivation_proof` that is neither `null` nor a string, and add mutation coverage for scalar and container proof values on every derived event group and runtime — is not present. `packages/schema/src/capability.ts` still only checks `derivation_proof !== null` for non-derived cells (line 587) and `isFilledString(cell.derivation_proof)` for the DERIVED-to-UNAVAILABLE fallback (line 598), with no type rejection; `packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts` still assigns only `null`, `""`, `"   "`, and a valid string as proof values, with no non-string mutation cases. Whether the task was completed is not the question I am answering, and an unchanged tree cannot implement a ruled-out approach it never introduced. Because approving an empty patch requires no one to revisit or re-explain the exact-count decision, the answer is COMPLIANT rather than INDETERMINATE: the record and the tree both point the same way, and there is no second plausible reading under which a floor-style lane count exists here.
